concept_summary: A reverse-loop game in the world of Gate Ledger: every gate you pass writes a debt or a credit that settles at the end of the run: you begin holding everything the source hands out and win by giving it all back. Where the source loop is 'A runner where each gate choice multiplies or adds to a squad value, so steering and quick arithmetic compete for the same attention', here every move undoes the 'A runner where each gate choice multiplies or adds to a squad value, so steering and quick arithmetic compete for the same attention' loop step by step instead of advancing it, so the map empties and the score falls. Hoarding triggers the lose state; the end screen celebrates an empty board.
first_experiment: Paper prototype: ten tokens stand in for everything the player owns and each turn must discard at least one; test with five players whether emptying the board feels like winning after three rounds.
source_idea_title: Gate Ledger: every gate you pass writes a debt or a credit that settles at the end of the run
why_it_is_opposite: While the source rewards accumulation (A runner where each gate choice multiplies or adds to a squad value, so steering and quick arithmetic compete for the same attention), this concept rewards the opposite: progress means having less, so a winning run here would score zero in the source.

concept_summary: The same core loop as Ink Debt: every stroke you draw is spent from a visible ink budget, and the level is built from what survives, rebuilt end to end for newcomers instead of its current crowd. Controls, difficulty, session shape, and rewards assume newcomers: a guided, jargon-free on-ramp for total beginners. Nothing in this build serves the old crowd; one client cannot satisfy both.
first_experiment: Take one level from the source fantasy, apply the inverted tuning only, and playtest with five target players for ten minutes; a quit-rate on the opposite side of half from the source baseline confirms the audience split is real.
source_idea_title: Ink Debt: every stroke you draw is spent from a visible ink budget, and the level is built from what survives
why_it_is_opposite: While the source is tuned for its current crowd (Mass mobile and desktop, non-gamers, social sharers: systems tuned for veterans of the genre), this concept flips every tuning decision toward newcomers (a guided, jargon-free on-ramp for total beginners), so the two builds want mutually exclusive players.

concept_summary: The fantasy of Bodycam browser slice: a first-person view that is a camera feed you can lose stretched over a single persistent season lasting months: one meaningful decision per evening, no grinding, no catching up. Progress compounds across real calendar time and a missed week bends the story instead of ending it. The finale is scheduled, shared, and unrepeatable.
first_experiment: Concierge test: run the core decision by hand over seven daily messages with three players; if day-seven return beats the source's second-session return, the long form has legs.
source_idea_title: Bodycam browser slice: a first-person view that is a camera feed you can lose
why_it_is_opposite: While the source fits short sessions, this concept flips the clock: one season here outlasts hundreds of source sessions, so the source habit of quick payoff actively hurts.
